prompt:
以下はある英語ニュースpodcast記事のFull Story・Point One・Point Twoです。
Point One・Point Twoそれぞれについて、以下6項目を判定してください
(それぞれPASS/FAIL)。

- qa_not_caveat_only: このPointが、研究上の限界・一般化上の注意・免責事項
  だけで構成されていない場合PASS(それらに加えて実質的な新しい内容がある
  場合もPASS。留保だけでPoint枠全体が終わっている場合はFAIL)
- qa_not_full_story_paraphrase: Full Storyの要約・言い換えに留まっていない
  場合PASS(Full Storyの中心的なlogic・結論を語彙だけ変えて繰り返している
  場合はFAIL)
- qa_not_other_point_paraphrase: もう一方のPointの要約・言い換えになって
  いない場合PASS
- qa_explains_why_it_matters: 「だから何なのか」を具体的に説明できている
  場合PASS(聞き手にとっての具体的な意味・示唆がある場合)
- qa_specific_not_generic: この記事のLedger固有の内容に基づいており、他の
  どんな記事にもほぼそのまま流用できる一般論になっていない場合PASS
- qa_adds_new_value: 新しい理解・解釈・意外性・具体的示唆のいずれかを
  実際に加えている場合PASS(Full Storyだけを聞いた場合と比べて、聞き手の
  理解が実際に深まっている場合)

reasoningには、判定理由を1〜2文の日本語で書いてください(特にFAILの場合は
具体的な理由を明記してください)。

【Full Story】
As of September 2026, a clear preference is emerging among some young people in Japan, especially young men. Travel is not only about seeing many places. More young travelers are showing interest in trips that leave room for their own interests and pace.

A 2025 survey found that men aged 29 and under ranked solo travel and hobby-focused travel among their top choices. Each was chosen by about one in four people. In a separate survey, about 90 percent of Japanese Gen Z respondents wanted free time during an overseas tour. About four in five wanted half a day or more.

But the calendar tells a less relaxed story.

When people were asked what they would do if they could take a month off, the most common answer was a trip of about one week. It was chosen by about 24 percent. Yet among people planning an autumn trip, the average stay was about two nights, with a median of two nights.

The Tourism Agency’s 2025 white paper still lists longer stays as a policy challenge. So the wish for slower, more personal travel is visible, but it has not become a clear change in how long people stay.

And the shift is not the same for everyone. Among women aged 29 and under, nearly 45 percent were still interested in visiting famous tourist sites. The picture is mixed, not a simple move from sightseeing to long stays.

【Point One】
The practical meaning of this preference is not “never join a tour” or “skip every famous place.” A young traveler may choose both while keeping part of the schedule for personal use. That might be a half-day of solo exploring or time for a hobby. The emerging model is a flexible mix, not an all-or-nothing choice.

【Point Two】
The duration figures should not be treated as one test of whether travel is becoming slower. One measure asks what people would choose under a month-long break. The other records plans being made now. A short trip may still allow a personal pace, while a hoped-for week may never happen. The evidence points to two tasks, not one verdict: support longer stays and improve the short trips people already take.

point_one.reasoning: 調査結果を単に繰り返すのではなく、観光地巡り・ツアーと個人の自由時間を両立させる「柔軟な混合型」という具体的な旅行モデルに落とし込んでいる。若い旅行者が実際にどう選択できるかが明確になり、記事の示唆を一段具体化している。

point_two.reasoning: 月単位の休暇での希望と、現在計画されている旅行期間を区別し、短期旅行にも個人のペースを組み込めるという実務的示唆を加えている点は有益。ただし、その二つの数字はFull Storyですでに明示的に対比され、「長期滞在への支援と短期旅行の改善が必要」という結論も、本文の『長期滞在への課題』と『実際の滞在期間は変わっていない』の言い換えに近いため、独立した新展開とは言いにくい。
